stories.title: As families retrieve bodies, Gaza is running out of places to bury the dead
stories.summary: Israel's genocidal war on Gaza has seen thousands of bodies buried in makeshift sites. Twenty-year-old Omar al-Sawhi has to find a burial place for his father, Mohammad, 40, who was shot dead close to the “Yellow Line”, an Israeli-designated military zone in Gaza. Mohammad, from the Zeitoun neighbourhood of Gaza City, was working at a small roadside stall selling tea and coffee when a bullet struck him in the neck on June 10, killing him almost instantly. Omar headed to the Zeitoun Cemetery to bury his father and found the graves tightly packed together, many of them victims of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. Many of them are marked with just a stone and a piece of paper attached bearing the name of the deceased, due to a lack of space and the difficult conditions caused by the war. “I stood in the middle of the cemetery and saw so many graves. There were mountains of sand, with people buried underneath,” Omar told Al Jazeera. “A grave was just a stone with a piece of paper bearing the name of the martyr, without the grave being built or properly prepared as it was before the war.” A grave here currently costs about 500 shekels ($167), a sum his family could not afford, so they had to find an alternative. “There was also no space for a new grave, so we had to bury him in my grandfather’s grave,” he said. The complete breakdown of services in Gaza and the dangers from Israeli attacks meant that thousands of dead Palestinians have been counted as “missing” during the war. Many of them were buried in gardens, or tents, or the grounds of camps for the displaced, schools or hospitals.
